title: Console usability study — customer feedback & action backlog
content:
Overview:
This is a synthesis doc from the Feb–Mar 2026 round of console usability sessions with customers and internal engineers. Primary goals: validate the new Route Detail panel wireframe, surface common pain points for model routing & rollout flows, and produce a prioritized action backlog for the next two sprints (Mar sprints). Sessions: 8 sessions (5 customers, 3 internal). Mix of enterprise (dedicated/private) and PLG dev users.

Method & participants:
- Moderated remote sessions, 45 mins each. Tasks + think-aloud + post-task SUS-ish rating.
- Participants: 3 platform engineers, 2 product engineers at customers, 2 solutions engineers, 1 internal SRE.
- Task set: 1) Create a canary rollout for model-v2 with fallback to model-v1; 2) Inspect per-route latency breakdown and attribute high tail latency; 3) Configure auto-bursting policy for Dedicated pool.
- Test assets: clickable low-fi wireframes (Route Detail v2) and small dataset for tracing. Recorded + timestamps available (link in linked_artifacts).

High-level findings (synthesis):
1) Mental model mismatch for rollouts: many participants expect "traffic split" to be on a percentage slider at route-level, but our wireframe exposes variant groups under an advanced section. Result: hesitation, task failure in 2/8 sessions until moderator prompted.
2) Hidden defaults caused surprises: default fallback to a smaller/cheaper quantized model was not visible in the rollout summary; two customers found it alarming when they realised runtime could swap to a different model family.
3) Latency attribution is useful but noisy: users love per-token heatmaps and per-token cost charts, but they want grouping by request type (streaming vs non-streaming) and better correlation with request metadata (region, batch size). Current mock showed raw token timelines only.
4) Autoscale policy semantics confusing: participants were uncertain what "burst capacity" buys — is it reserved GPUs, a warmup queue, or instant preemptible instances? This led to conservative configurations or callers asking for SRE help.
5) Discoverability problem for rollout history & audit: two participants tried to find the last failed canary run and had to drill through multiple menus. They expect an inline history chip on the route page.

Representative quotes (verbatim where possible):
- "I thought percentage would be on the main screen — I kept looking for it, assumed it's not supported." (Customer-PE-1)
- "If the UI hides fallback model details, I'm not comfortable enabling auto-fallback in production." (Customer-Platform-2)
- "This chart is nice but I need to click a few times to connect it to the request types — can we show the request tag next to the timeline?" (Internal-SRE)

Quantitative notes (small-N, directional):
- Task completion: Canary rollout creation success 6/8 without help; 2 needed moderator hints.
- Time-on-task (median): rollout task 9m, latency attribution 6m, autoscale config 11m.
- Post-task confidence (1–5): rollout 3.6, latency 4.1, autoscale 2.8.

Wireframe-specific feedback (Route Detail v2):
- Positive: single-pane summary with quick toggles (on/off) for rollouts appreciated. Users liked the mocked "impact estimate" badge next to each variant.
- Needs work: the rollout summary card currently truncates model variant metadata (quantization, accelerator type). Request: expose a compact metadata row (GPU/CPU, q8/q4, params) inline.
- Suggestion: make a small info icon that explains fallback semantics (what triggers it, notification behavior).

Usability issues mapped to backlog items (prioritized):
P0 (must-fix before public rollout):
- BACKLOG-1001: Surface traffic split control on primary Route Detail card (UX change). Add a percentage slider + numeric input next to variant list. Acceptance criteria: a user can set traffic split without opening 'advanced'. Estimates: 3 (design) + 5 (frontend) + 3 (backend coupling).
- BACKLOG-1002: Expose fallback model metadata in rollout summary and add "fallback details" hover. Acceptance criteria: fallback model family and quantization level visible; tooltip explains policy. Estimates: 2 + 4.

P1 (important, can follow):
- BACKLOG-1003: Autoscale / Burst documentation + inline explanation microcopy. Clarify what "burst capacity" is and cost/latency tradeoffs. Acceptance criteria: documentation in Console + a one-line help text and link to the dedicated docs page. Estimates: 1 (content) + 2 (frontend).
- BACKLOG-1004: Rollout history quick-chip on Route Detail showing last 5 runs with status badges and links to logs. Acceptance criteria: last 5 entries displayed, clickable to open run detail. Estimates: 4 + 3.

P2 (nice-to-have):
- BACKLOG-1005: Latency attribution: add request-type grouping layers and a filter to color by region. Acceptance criteria: users can toggle grouping and see filtered timeline. Estimates: 5.
- BACKLOG-1006: Add a "preview impact" simulation that applies a traffic split to a small synthetic trace to show projected TPS/cost. Acceptance criteria: simulation runs within 10s for small traces and returns cost delta. Estimates: 6.

Open questions / design tradeoffs:
- Do we prioritize exposing every model metadata inline (space/visual noise) or rely on a compact summary + hover? Recommendation: compact inline row with toggle "show details" (keeps default simple).
- Notification model for fallback: should fallback trigger an automatic alert to owners or only be surfaced in audit logs? Customers asked for optional immediate notification. Proposed: default to log + opt-in alert channel (email/slack).
- How to handle percentage split accessibility (keyboard, screen reader)? Need a11y review and ARIA semantics for the slider control.

Quick wins (1–2 day tasks):
- Add microcopy under "Burst capacity" explaining the three behaviours (reserved, warm, preemptible) with a link out to docs — tag to content team.
- Move the traffic-split control to top-level variant card (frontend tweak) — short spike to verify no backend changes required.

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- Radhika: prioritize P0/P1 in next grooming meeting (Mar 12).
- Marco: prototype top-level traffic-split control (Mar 5–9) and post prototype in #console-design for quick feedback.
- Sasha: write microcopy for autoscale/burst and fallback tooltip (due Mar 8).
- Elena: raise PR for route history chip data model (backend scope check) and link PR in linked_artifacts.

Notes to self / rough follow-ups:
- Create a short follow-up survey for participants to capture longer-term adoption signals (Do they use fallback after 1 month?).
- Capture an example of a "surprising fallback" from Customer-Platform-2 to use in changelog and in-app tooltip wording.
- Schedule a 30-min design review with engineering to ensure rollback UX is covered in error states.

Appendix (session-level highlights):
- Customer-PE-1: Wanted presets for common rollout patterns (10/90, 50/50, blue/green). Suggested a small dropdown next to slider.
- Customer-Platform-2: Strong on visibility; insisted on explicit confirmation modal when fallback to a model family with lower privacy guarantees is possible.
- Internal-SRE: Asked for logs to include request-level tags to aid latency correlation.

Files & artifacts produced:
- Lo-fi wireframes: Route-Detail-v2.pdf (attached in design Figma — see linked_artifacts page).
- Session recordings: stored on internal drive (link in Slack thread).
- Sketches: low-fi hand-sketched flow included at end of design doc (uploaded).

If you want, I can split the P0 items into discrete tickets with acceptance criteria and example screenshots for the groomer packet.

Unresolved: we still need clarity from legal on how much model metadata we can expose for licensed models in private deployments — tagged legal-ask.
